name: Emmanuel Macron
description: French president associated with European integration, market-oriented reform and public investment.
scope: Public positions and conduct during the specified period; this represents the individual rather than all party members or citizens.

axes.brief: Competitive elections and constitutional review continued under a strong presidency.
axes.counter: Article 49.3 bypassed a parliamentary vote but remained subject to a no-confidence procedure.

axes.brief: Protest policing and counter-terrorism measures emphasised order alongside civil rights.
axes.counter: Constitutional review and freedom of opposition persisted.

axes.brief: Republican integration and secular public institutions favoured a shared civic identity.
axes.counter: Recognition of diverse origins did not grant every religious accommodation.

axes.brief: Managed migration combined work routes with stronger removal powers.
axes.counter: Judicial rejection of some restrictions limits attribution of the entire proposed law.

axes.brief: Military capability and intervention accompanied European security cooperation.
axes.counter: Diplomacy and negotiated settlement remained priorities; supporting defence is not unlimited war.

axes.brief: European integration and pooled authority qualified national autonomy.
axes.counter: Independent French deterrence and strategic autonomy remained important.

axes.brief: Privatisation and business investment coexisted with public health and strategic enterprises.
axes.counter: EDF renationalisation is a substantial strategic exception.

axes.brief: European common trade rules and open investment favoured trade.
axes.counter: European strategic autonomy and safeguards qualified unconditional openness.

axes.brief: Market-oriented labour reform coexisted with industrial incentives and a legal wage floor.
axes.counter: France retained substantial public coordination and regulated essential sectors.

axes.brief: Tax and pension reforms prioritised investment and fiscal sustainability.
axes.counter: Benefits and crisis assistance persisted; this is relative preference rather than abolition of welfare.

axes.brief: Secular republican civil authority remained the legal foundation.
axes.counter: Religious heritage and holidays persisted without clerical legislative control.

axes.brief: Marriage equality, assisted reproduction and constitutional abortion protection reflected social reform.
axes.counter: Age and consent limits and family preferences qualify every possible extension.

axes.brief: Nuclear power, infrastructure and technical industry were promoted.
axes.counter: Medical and ecosystem risks retained regulation; no exact enhancement response is documented.

axes.brief: National institutions directed taxation, education and public policy.
axes.counter: Corsican autonomy discussions and regional government supply counter-evidence.

axes.brief: Education and opportunity policy supply contextual social explanations.
axes.counter: No comprehensive heredity doctrine was located; these comparisons have low confidence.
